correctness.rationale: The independent integer census ranges over all 3^6 labeled rules, verifies 288 primitive rules by support growth through power 5, and matches all 16 pair-matrix characteristic-polynomial rows. Theorem B uses the raw pair matrix only at height one. Height is coprime to two and bounded by three, since the height classes have disjoint nonempty letter supports, so the only exception is height three, which forces a 3-cycle. The substitution maps that orbit to itself; using substitution-shift covariance with shift multiplier two, there is a unique fixed phase modulo three. In that phase its rule is (ab,ca,bc) on (a,b,c). Each of the six rules is primitive and has height three; all are in the indicated 18-rule raw Perron-2 row. Reassigning them to complexity zero leaves 42 infinite-complexity rules. The 12 nilpotent pair matrices give the other finite systems. Factoring the remaining polynomials and checking signs in the three named cubics gives 1 < sqrt(2) < alpha < phi < beta < tau < 2. The complexity transform is strictly increasing on these rates and sends sqrt(2) to 2. This proves the exact eight counts, the sharp gap, and, via Theorem A, the 114 versus 174 tame/null split.
residual_risks: The infinite-dynamics theorem is imported, not independently reproved. A literal length bound on height in Remark 2.16 is inconsistent with the period-three example; the proof uses only the alphabet-size bound and coprimality.

originality.rationale: The supported claim is the joint exact finite spectrum, multiplicities and sharp gap on all labeled ternary length-two primitive rules, not the general spectral formula or a new dynamical criterion. The closest checked general theorem computes a per-rule rate and treats the pure base; it gives no explicit attainable-rate list, aggregate counts or gap on this subclass without new exhaustive classification and finite-height accounting. The strongest distinct indexed findings are both substantively different. This is a bounded best-of-knowledge judgment, not a historical priority claim.
residual_risks: A specialized enumeration under terms such as coincidence/disagreement matrices or automatic symbolic dynamics may exist outside the retrieved material. Empty broad search results and ranked-search misses do not prove absence.
